title: Newton's Inequality (n = 3), Sign-Agnostic via an Explicit SOS Certificate
description: A complementary, sharpened treatment of the k = 2 Newton rung S₂² ≥ S₁S₃ (log-concavity of the elementary symmetric means) in the concrete case n = 3. The general-n, all-k Newton log-concavity is ALREADY formalized in the gallery for NONNEGATIVE reals (AmgmInequalityOQ02OQ02.lean: elemSymm_log_concave, newton_log_concavity_proved), so this is not a first proof. Its added value is threefold, all specific to n = 3: (1) it is SIGN-AGNOSTIC — for reals a,b,c with e₁=a+b+c, e₂=ab+bc+ca, e₃=abc, the inequality e₂² ≥ 3·e₁·e₃ (equivalently S₂² ≥ S₁S₃) holds for ALL reals, dropping the nonnegativity hypothesis the general inductive proof carries; (2) it exhibits the EXPLICIT sum-of-squares witness e₂² − 3e₁e₃ = ½[(ab−bc)² + (bc−ca)² + (ca−ab)²], a pure ring identity; (3) it characterizes the EQUALITY locus ab = bc = ca. 5 theorems, 3 definitions, 0 axioms.

Demonstrates that at n = 3 Newton's inequality is exactly a three-term sum of squares, discharged by ring + nlinarith with no induction, no nonnegativity, and none of the Rolle/derivative machinery — a self-contained elementary and sharper-hypothesis proof for this size

overview.historicalContext: Isaac Newton observed that the elementary symmetric means S_k = e_k / C(n,k) of n real numbers are log-concave: S_k² ≥ S_{k-1}·S_{k+1} for 1 ≤ k ≤ n−1. These Newton inequalities refine and interpolate the Maclaurin chain S₁ ≥ √S₂ ≥ ∛S₃ ≥ ⋯, whose two ends recover AM ≥ GM. Unlike Maclaurin's inequalities, Newton's inequalities hold for ALL real tuples (not only nonnegative ones), because their classical proof runs through Rolle's theorem: the derivative of a real-rooted polynomial is again real-rooted, and iterating down to a quadratic reduces log-concavity to the nonnegativity of a discriminant. The general-n, all-k log-concavity is already formalized in this gallery — for nonnegative reals — in amgm-inequality-oq-02-oq-02 (theorems elemSymm_log_concave and newton_log_concavity_proved, by induction on n). This entry is a complementary refinement for n = 3: it removes the nonnegativity hypothesis (the SOS certificate is sign-agnostic), makes the sum-of-squares witness explicit, and pins down the equality locus — none of which the general inductive proof provides.
overview.problemStatement: For reals $a,b,c$ let $e_1 = a+b+c$, $e_2 = ab+bc+ca$, $e_3 = abc$, and the symmetric means $S_1 = e_1/3$, $S_2 = e_2/3$, $S_3 = e_3$. Then $S_2^2 \ge S_1 S_3$, equivalently the cleared form $e_2^2 \ge 3\,e_1 e_3$.
overview.text: The proof rests on a single algebraic identity: the Newton defect equals half a sum of three squares, e₂² − 3e₁e₃ = ½[(ab−bc)² + (bc−ca)² + (ca−ab)²]. Nonnegativity of the right-hand side (three squares) immediately gives the cleared inequality e₂² ≥ 3e₁e₃ for all reals. The averaged form S₂² ≥ S₁S₃ follows by dividing through by the positive constant 9 (the denominators C(3,k) are constants, so no positivity hypotheses on a,b,c are needed). The SOS certificate also reads off the equality case: equality holds iff all three pairwise products ab, bc, ca are equal.
overview.proofStrategy: Three moves. (1) newton_sos_identity: expand e₂² − 3e₁e₃ and match it term-by-term to ½[(ab−bc)² + (bc−ca)² + (ca−ab)²] — a pure `ring` identity after unfolding the definitions. (2) newton_cleared: since the right-hand side of the identity is a sum of squares, `nlinarith` with the three `sq_nonneg` hints (and the identity) closes e₂² ≥ 3e₁e₃. (3) newton_base_step: the averaged defect (e₂/3)² − (e₁/3)·(e₃/1) equals (e₂² − 3e₁e₃)/9 by `ring`, and the numerator is ≥ 0 by step (2), so `div_nonneg` + `linarith` finish. The equality direction newton_eq_of_all_eq (a=b=c ⇒ equality) is a direct `ring` computation; the converse newton_products_eq_of_eq extracts ab=bc=ca from the vanishing sum of squares via `pow_eq_zero_iff`.
keyInsights: At n = 3, Newton's inequality is literally a three-term sum of squares. The defect e₂² − 3e₁e₃ equals ½[(ab−bc)² + (bc−ca)² + (ca−ab)²], so the inequality is an SOS certificate — no Rolle's theorem, no discriminants, no real-rootedness argument is needed at this size.

This rung is strictly beyond Cauchy-Schwarz. The base rung S₁² ≥ S₂ reduces to the power-mean bound n·p₂ ≥ e₁² (Cauchy-Schwarz). The k = 2 rung has no such reduction; its content is the genuinely new SOS above, which is why the parent's open-question flagged it as the first rung requiring more than Cauchy-Schwarz.

No nonnegativity is required. Although Maclaurin's chain assumes nonnegative reals, S₂² ≥ S₁S₃ holds for all real a,b,c because the SOS certificate is sign-agnostic. The nonnegativity hypothesis only becomes essential at Maclaurin rungs where one extracts real roots (√S₂, ∛S₃, …).

The equality locus is exactly ab = bc = ca. Because the defect is a sum of squares of the pairwise differences of the products, equality forces those products to coincide — recovering a = b = c for nonzero variables, the expected extremal configuration.

This is a complementary refinement, not a first proof: the general-n, all-k Newton log-concavity is already formalized for nonnegative reals in amgm-inequality-oq-02-oq-02 (elemSymm_log_concave / newton_log_concavity_proved, by induction on n). The delta here — sign-agnostic (all reals) at n=3, plus the explicit SOS witness and equality locus — is exactly what the induction does not give.

The sign-agnostic general-n statement is the open frontier: cleared of binomial denominators it reads 2(n−2)·e₂² ≥ 3(n−1)·e₁e₃ for all reals, reducing to e₂² ≥ 3e₁e₃ at n = 3. Removing nonnegativity in general n needs the Rolle/derivative real-rootedness argument (or a general SOS witness); that remains the forward open question.
prerequisites: Elementary symmetric polynomials e₁, e₂, e₃ of three reals
Symmetric means S_k = e_k / C(n,k) and Newton's log-concavity S_k² ≥ S_{k-1}S_{k+1}
That x² = 0 ⇒ x = 0 over a field (pow_eq_zero_iff) for the equality characterization

conclusion.implications: Sharpens the known n=3 case of Newton's k=2 inequality in three ways the general inductive proof (elemSymm_log_concave, valid only for nonnegative reals) does not: (1) the SOS certificate holds for all reals, so the nonnegativity hypothesis is unnecessary at n=3; (2) newton_sos_identity is a reusable standalone algebraic witness; (3) the equality locus ab = bc = ca is characterized. The natural next target is to remove nonnegativity in general n — the sign-agnostic form 2(n−2)e₂² ≥ 3(n−1)e₁e₃ — whose classical proof goes through Rolle's theorem.
openQuestions: Prove the SIGN-AGNOSTIC general-n k = 2 Newton inequality 2(n−2)·e₂² ≥ 3(n−1)·e₁e₃ for all reals (n ≥ 3), removing the nonnegativity hypothesis of the existing gallery proof (elemSymm_log_concave). The classical route is Rolle's theorem: derivatives of a real-rooted polynomial are real-rooted, reducing to a quadratic discriminant; formalizing that ∏(x − xᵢ)' is real-rooted is the crux.
Extend the sign-agnostic n=4 rungs (S₂² ≥ S₁S₃ and S₃² ≥ S₂S₄) via explicit SOS certificates, testing how far the elementary all-reals SOS approach reaches before Rolle's theorem becomes unavoidable.
Give a general-n explicit SOS witness for e₂² − 3·(n−1)/(2·(n−2))·e₁e₃ (if one exists), which would supply an induction-free, sign-agnostic proof matching the n=3 certificate here.
